    Proposition 5.4 in its general form #

    mesh-deformations.tex (prop:filtered-normal-form): "Let C = kQ/(r_1, …, r_t) be a finite-dimensional graded algebra over any field, with Q finite and each r_i homogeneous quadratic. For q ≥ 3, let D_{q-1} send a family (f_a)_a, where f_a ∈ C_{q-1} is parallel to the arrow a, to the family whose ith entry is the sum, over the arrow occurrences in r_i, of the terms obtained by replacing that occurrence of a by f_a; these entries lie in C_q. Assume that D_{q-1} is surjective for every q ≥ 3. Let E be a finite filtered algebra, or a finite filtered category with the vertices of Q as objects, with a specified graded identification gr E = C. Then E is isomorphic to C by a map inducing that identification."

    Here C is the relation category of the quadratic relations r_i (Rel), E a k-linear category with objects O x (x a vertex), a finite multiplicative filtration F of its Hom spaces and symbols σ_d : F^d → C_d realizing gr E = C (FilteredId). The proof is the source's: lift the arrows (Lifts); the relation errors lie in F³; a degree-q error is D_{q-1} of a family, and subtracting its lifts cancels it, the terms with two corrections having degree 2q - 2 > q (exists_correction); the filtration is finite, so the errors vanish; the resulting functor C → E is bijective on Hom spaces by graded injectivity and surjectivity (normalForm). The case E = ind(mod A), C = k(Γ_A) is IndSkeleton.filteredNormalForm.
